source.title: Geometry-induced Regularization in Deep ReLU Neural Networks
source.authors: Joachim Bona-Pellissier; François Malgouyres; Franccois Bachoc

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a width sweep on MNIST where test error continues to fall after training error reaches zero, extending the width/generalization question to a four-layer fully connected network. It does not test the one-hidden-layer settings named in V2.
record.gate_note: The reported width-sweep results and local-dimension measurements are included. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 7.2 tests V2 in a new architecture: three hidden ReLU layers on MNIST. After training error reaches zero at width 12, test error decreases from 0.101 to 0.058 at width 85.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify local dimension as a geometry-induced regularity criterion, connect it to their notions of flatness and optimization dynamics, and demonstrate related behavior on MNIST training and test samples. They explicitly leave a formal connection to generalization guarantees open.
record.recipe_differences: The width sweep addresses generalization beyond zero training error, but uses a four-layer fully connected MNIST classifier rather than the one-hidden-layer settings in V2; no explicit regularization is specified.
record.method_sensitivity: The rank comparison changes with width: training and test ranks are nearly equal below 21 185 parameters, then diverge. During training, training-sample rank falls more steeply than test-sample rank.

fits_no_version.finding: Training and test local-dimension ranks are nearly equal below width 25, diverge for larger networks, and grow more slowly than maximum rank. Both ranks decrease during training at width 30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On this MNIST setup, learned ReLU networks exhibit reduced local functional dimension on both training and test inputs, with stronger reductions relative to maximum rank in larger networks.

record.problems: The MNIST test sample is larger than the training sample and is also used to estimate local dimension. Numerical uncertainty estimates are not stated in the supplied text; the width-sweep rank and error curves are presented in Figure 9.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the comparison of held-out performance under natural and random labels.

One-hidden-layer networks and downsampled CIFAR-10. Training uses a fixed 1,000 epochs rather than demonstrated convergence at every width. No explicit regularizer is described, but its absence is not explicitly confirmed.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations of the training recipe.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized training examples versus random removal followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V2. Its discussion of flatness uses a different construct from V7 and supplies no test of V7. Numerical uncertainty or repeated-run variability is not reported for the width sweep.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
One-hidden-layer networks, downsampled CIFAR-10, and the explicit no-regularization condition.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Large versus small batch comparisons and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.subject: fully-connected feed-forward ReLU network; widths (784, w, w, w, 10)
rows.operation_detail: Increased width from 1 to 85; training error reached 0 at w=12 and remained 0 thereafter.

conditions.value: MNIST; 6 000 training images and 20 000 test images
stochastic gradient descent, learning rate 0.1, batch size 256

rows.note: At w=12, training error is 0; the text states test error continues to decrease as width increases.
rows.check: The numbers and conditions are correct. This row establishes the zero-training-error threshold and comparison baseline; evidence for improvement with further widening comes from R2.

conditions.value: MNIST; 6 000 training images and 20 000 test images
stochastic gradient descent, learning rate 0.1, batch size 256

rows.note: The text reports the test-error decrease from w=12 to w=85 after training error has reached 0.

rows.subject: fully-connected feed-forward ReLU network; widths (784, w, w, w, 10)
rows.size_stated: widths w<25; exact parameter counts vary by width
rows.operation_detail: Compared local dimension on the training and test samples.
rows.value: The ranks are nearly equal when the number of parameters is smaller than 21 185 (w=25); both are not far from maximum rank for w<25.
rows.note: The text describes rank behavior, not magnitude-aware sharpness or a direct measure of the train-test error gap.
rows.check: The rank finding is reported correctly, but local dimension does not measure any listed version's effect. Its occurrence cannot establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness relation.

rows.subject: fully-connected feed-forward ReLU network; widths (784, w, w, w, 10)
rows.operation_detail: Compared local dimension on the training and test samples as width increased.
rows.baseline: The ranks are nearly equal below 21 185 parameters.
rows.value: A gap appears between the ranks; both increase less and less with parameter count, while maximum rank is nearly proportional to parameter count.
rows.note: The paper says the rank gap grows with network size; this is not the train-test error gap named in V7.
rows.check: Local-dimension ranks do not measure any listed version. Also, w=25 has exactly 21,185 parameters: the recorded condition w≥25 should say at least 21,185 parameters. The source itself inconsistently combines a strict parameter inequality with w≥25.

rows.subject: fully-connected feed-forward ReLU network; widths (784, 30, 30, 30, 10)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked local dimension on the training and test samples during training.
rows.value: Training-sample rank consistently decreases during training; test-sample rank also decreases, with a more gentle slope.
rows.note: The paper reports these rank trends alongside falling test error; it does not establish that this is the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
rows.check: The rank trend is reported correctly, but neither decreasing local dimension nor its transfer to test inputs measures the magnitude-scaled perturbation sharpness named in V7.
